name: Laurent Panifous
party: Libertés, Indépendants, Outre-mer et Territoires (LIOT); ex-Parti socialiste (until 2022)
bio: Laurent Panifous, born 21 December 1976 in Foix (Ariège), is a French politician serving as Minister-Delegate to the Prime Minister, in charge of Relations with Parliament, in the government of Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu. He was first appointed to this post on 12 October 2025 (in the second Lecornu government) and retained it in the government reshuffle confirmed by decree of 26 February 2026. A trained director of health and social-care establishments (he ran EHPAD retirement homes in Ariège from 2000 to 2022), he holds a Master 2 in health law from the University of Toulouse. Locally he was mayor of Le Fossat from 2014 to 2022 and president of the communauté de communes Arize-Lèze from 2017 to 2022. A Socialist Party dissident who refused the 2022 NUPES alliance with La France Insoumise, he was elected deputy for Ariège's 2nd constituency in 2022 and re-elected in 2024. In February 2025 he was elected president of the LIOT group (Libertés, Indépendants, Outre-mer et Territoires) at the National Assembly. As a deputy he was notably co-rapporteur of the bill on the right to assisted dying (aide à mourir). His entry into a government he described as not sharing 'the ideas of Macronism' drew criticism from parts of the left.
